title: Canary failover deadlock from stale shard pins during traffic surge — follow-up & eviction plan
creator: Sofia Ruiz
description: During a high-traffic spike on 2026-03-09 we observed a canary-to-primary failover that entered a deadlock state. Several shard sets remained pinned to the retiring canary version due to stale pin metadata and an eviction race with autoscaler leases. The result was elevated 95th/99th percentile latencies for a subset of customers, partial request failures routed to overloaded backends, and an inability to roll back the canary safely until manual eviction completed. This ticket captures the incident summary, immediate mitigations, and a concrete plan to prevent shard pin deadlocks in future rollouts.
timeline: 2026-03-09T02:14:00Z - Canary promotion triggered for model v2026-03-08-canary-3
2026-03-09T02:16:30Z - Traffic spike from internal load test + customer rollout; autoscaler attempted scale-up
2026-03-09T02:17:10Z - Health flapping reported for several shards; orchestrator began failover
2026-03-09T02:18:05Z - Route translator moved traffic but some shard metadata still pinned to canary version
2026-03-09T02:19:40Z - Autoscaler lease renewals conflicted with eviction job; eviction retries stalled
2026-03-09T02:23:50Z - Latency and error-rate alerting escalated to on-call
2026-03-09T02:35:00Z - Emergency runbook: manual force-evict executed on 6 shardsets; traffic normalized
2026-03-09T03:02:00Z - Temporary rollback completed; canary disabled pending investigation
detection: Automated SLO alert from console (p99 latency > 800ms for route /v1/generate) and increased 5xx rate. On-call noticed correlated increase in route misroutes in tracing dashboard.
root_cause: Stale pin metadata on shard manifests combined with an eviction job that required acquiring an autoscaler lease. Under surge, lease handoff failed for several shard managers causing eviction retries to back off indefinitely. The orchestrator's promotion logic didn't clear pin references atomically, leaving mixed-serve state that blocked safe rollback and prevented automated recovery.
mitigations: Immediate: manual force-evict on affected shardsets to unblock routing and restore capacity
Short-term: disabled automatic promotion for the affected rollout pipeline until pin metadata guard is patched
Monitoring: added temporary dashboard with pin-age histogram and eviction retry counts to detect recurrence
action_items: ENG: implement atomic pin-unlink/swap in orchestrator promotion path to avoid transient mixed-serve states — owner: Ethan Blake — due: 2026-03-20
ENG: decouple eviction worker from autoscaler lease for critical fast-path evictions; add fallback lease-free eviction mode with conservative limits — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-04-03
ENG: add metric 'shard.pin_age_seconds' and an alert when > 120s for active shards — owner: Samir Patel — due: 2026-03-17
ENG: run a rollout chaos test that simulates surge + lease contention once patch is deployed — owner: QA Team (automations) — due: 2026-04-10
DOCS: update rollout runbook to include force-eviction checklist and safety TTLs — owner: Lina Park — due: 2026-03-18
followup_notes: We observed the autoscaler lease contention only under combined internal load test + partial customer ramp; standalone load tests did not reproduce reliably.
Patch should be gated behind canary in staging and a 48-hour soak with synthetic ramp; do not release to prod without the new metrics enabled.
Consider retrofitting older runtimes with a lightweight eviction shim to reduce blast radius for customers on legacy shard allocations.
